ops.old: BPCI was notable for being prospective in Model 2 (a single retrospective reconciliation payment) and retrospective in Models 3 and 4.
ops.new: Models 1 through 3 were retrospective — providers were paid fee-for-service and then reconciled against a target price — while Model 4 was prospective, paying a single lump sum for the hospital stay, physician services, and related readmissions.
ops.claim: Original BPCI prospective in Model 2, retrospective in Models 3 and 4
ops.sources: CMS fact sheet 'Bundled Payments for Care Improvement Initiative (BPCI)' (2015-08-13; 2016-04-18): Models 1-3 retrospective, Model 4 prospective; Model 1 began April 2013, Models 2-4 October 2013

ops.old: The 12-18 month lag between episode completion and reconciliation payment creates significant cash flow management challenges.
ops.new: The months-long lag between episode completion and reconciliation payment — BPCI-Advanced reconciled semiannually, after claims for each performance period had run out — creates significant cash flow management challenges.
ops.claim: 12-18 month lag between episode completion and reconciliation
ops.sources: CMS BPCI Advanced model page/participation agreement: semiannual reconciliation; no source for a 12-18 month lag

ops.old: All current CMS bundled payment models are voluntary, meaning hospitals and physician groups choose whether to participate.
ops.new: BPCI and BPCI-Advanced were voluntary, meaning hospitals and physician groups chose whether to participate.
ops.claim: All current CMS bundled payment models are voluntary
ops.sources: CMS TEAM model page: mandatory Transforming Episode Accountability Model for selected acute care hospitals, began 2026-01-01

ops.old: The Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement (CJR) model, launched in 2016, was the first and only mandatory bundled payment model in Medicare history, covering hip and knee replacement in selected geographic markets.
ops.new: The Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement (CJR) model, which ran from April 2016 through December 31, 2024, was Medicare's first mandatory bundled payment model to take effect, covering hip and knee replacement in selected geographic markets; TEAM, which began January 1, 2026, is its mandatory successor.
ops.claim: CJR was the first and only mandatory bundled payment model in Medicare history
ops.sources: CMS CJR model page (performance period 2016-04-01 to 2024-12-31; three-year extension final rule, Federal Register 2021-05-03); CMS TEAM page (mandatory, began 2026-01-01)

ops.old: Remedy Partners (acquired by Nuvera), Archway Health, Caravan Health, and several large health systems
ops.new: Signify Health (into which Remedy Partners, a major convener since the original BPCI, merged in 2019) — the largest BPCI-Advanced convener by episodes managed — Archway Health, and several large health systems
ops.claim: Conveners: Remedy Partners (acquired by Nuvera), Archway Health, Caravan Health
ops.sources: Signify Health Form S-1 (2021) and 10-K FY2021 (SEC EDGAR): largest BPCI-A convener by episodes; Remedy Partners became a BPCI-A Convener Participant 2018-10-01 and combined with Signify Health in 2019; Becker's 'The value of partnering with a convener' (Archway Health)
ops.note: No Nuvera acquisition exists; Caravan Health (an MSSP ACO enabler) not documented as a BPCI-A convener, removed.
